To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the best efforts for the QoS-assurance in dynamic reconfigurable dataflow systems are: (1) to ensure global consistency for all transactions in a system; (2) to use a reconfiguration protocol with a low number of messages; (3) to use a state transfer strategy with a low number and size of state messages; and (4) to use a benchmark for evaluating the QoS-assurances of different reconfiguration protocols and state transfer strategies.
QoS-assurance can be achieved by the use of the DynaQOS-CR (DynaQoS©-Controlled Reconfiguration) approach.

(1) the QoS of dynamic reconfiguration can be guaranteed if the reconfigured system is globally consistent and the necessary and sufficient condition for the consistency of the reconfigured system can be satisfied; (2) the QoS-assurance overhead can be minimized if the reconfigured dataflow system is stateless, and (3) the QoS can be assured if the reconfigured stateful dataflow system is consistent.
